Sida utgår från Sveriges Regering styrning av utvecklingssamarbete (bistånd).
Regering understryker att svenskt bistånd ska skapa förutsättningar för
bättre levnadsvillkor för människor som lever i fattigdom och förtryck.
Utvecklingssamarbetet har en viktig roll i att verka för fria och välfungerande
demokratiska samhällen. Regering ser potential i att hitta synergier mellan

våld. Det är en viktig del av vårt breda engagemang för global hälsa.

oavsett kön, ålder, sexuell läggning eller religion är en frihetsfråga.
Sveriges uppfattning är att för att kunna nyttja potentialen i ny digital teknik krävs
säker och betrodd infrastruktur, både för individens och för myndighetens
kommunikation.

activities.title: Setting up collaborations between iCog Labs Ethiopia and Dutch stakeholders in the IT and AI sectors
activities.description: Miss Betelhem Dessie is Ethiopia’s youngest tech pioneer and according to Quartz Africa one of the young African innovators to watch. She is the co-founder of iCog Labs, an Ethiopian software company focusing on artificial intelligence, IT, and social entrepreneurship.Through different programmes, the company supports programming skills development amongst Ethiopian youth and challenges them to come up with digital solutions for challenges faced in their hometowns.Since technical expertise is still hard to find in Ethiopia, this project supports iCog Labs and Betelhem Dessie by connecting them to Dutch companies, non-governmental organisations NGOs, and knowledge institutions to build on future collaborations.

activities.title: Digital Skills Training for South-African Women
activities.description: The fourth industrial revolution comes with a whole new sector of jobs. These jobs need specific skills and competencies and many of them, both in-country and abroad, are left unfilled. By providing tailor-made training on high-level digital skills (e.g. data science, AI, blockchain engineering), young female graduates will have better chances in the South African digital economy. They will have access to jobs that are now predominately occupied by men. Alternatively, the bourgeoning digital economy in South Africa will have access to local talent that is increasingly sought after.

activities.title: Nairobi: Cyber data protection – a study on (In)security in Kenya's Cyber-Space integration of artificial intelligence
activities.description: The aim of the Cyber data protection project is to execute a study on the security of Kenya's Cyber-Space integration of artificial intelligence. This is currently very relevant as both the private and public sectors are starting to incorporate artificial intelligence in their work. The proper use of artificial intelligence and protection of cyber data is therefore important for the future development of the tech-sector and tech legislation in Kenya.

activities.title: Solution Networks Program
activities.description:
Artificial intelligence (AI) holds great potential to revolutionize everything from how farmers increase their crop yields, to how governments communicate with their citizens in their own languages during natural disasters, to how healthcare providers respond to global pandemics. However, these benefits are accompanied by potential threats to privacy, data misuse, and algorithmic bias that could exacerbate marginalization. There is a need to identify key governance and norms related to AI and to propose policies to address the complex challenges associated with emerging technologies. 

This project proposes to strengthen policy advice, connections, and capacity in the Canadian and Global South AI ecosystems by engaging experts from across geographic, sectoral, and disciplinary boundaries on AI and governance. Solution networks would be created as collaborative opportunities for international teams of up to six individuals to develop approaches and applications that address current challenges and opportunities in the implementation of beneficial and responsible AI, such as inclusion by design, ethical by design, and green by design. activities.title: AI Governance and Policy Capacity Convenings between UK and Kenya
activities.description: This project strengthens cooperation between the UK, Kenya and wider African partners to improve skills and coordination on responsible artificial intelligence. It brings together government officials, experts and civil society to exchange knowledge through research, regional meetings and a Kenya–UK policy exchange visit. The project supports the creation of thematic groups that develop practical guidance for public service, agriculture, health and other priority areas. By improving access to reliable information and promoting inclusive participation, it helps governments make informed decisions, contribute to global discussions and sustain long-term capacity for safe and development-focused use of artificial intelligence.

activities.title: Techrun 2025-AI Digital and Sports Forum
activities.description: The project seeks to position Kenya—particularly Eldoret—as a leading African hub for AI-driven digital innovation by integrating technology, investment, youth skills development, and sports through the TechRun 2025 Forum. It aims to connect startups with investors, policymakers, and global partners while expanding youth access to AI and digital skills. By strengthening UK–Kenya collaboration on ethical AI, innovation capacity, and inclusive economic growth, the project will foster a sustainable pipeline of skilled youth, scalable startups, and long-term multi-stakeholder partnerships.

activities.title: Gen AI for Gen Z: Inspiring new generation of AI creators
activities.description:
Despite growing excitement about AI, Cambodia faces low understanding and experience in applying these powerful tools. The need to address biases and ethical AI use early is crucial for responsible applications. Currently, only 10% of Cambodian students choose IT fields, creating a significant gap in the country's AI readiness."GenAI for Gen Z" is a unique educational program designed to target Cambodian youth, ensuring at least 50% female participation. This project will introduce the transformative power of Generative AI, sparking a shift within Cambodian students. By bringing diverse genders together, we foster open discussions and understanding. We 
specifically target students from social and humanitarian sciences—particularly women—to inspire them with AI's potential, unleashing new possibilities for collaboration and creative applications.
As a leader in innovation and STEM support, the UK can play a pivotal role in fostering Cambodia's AI future. Funding this project helps bridge a knowledge gap, promotes inclusivity and responsible AI development, empowers underrepresented students, and inspires a new generation of tech creators in Cambodia. activities.title: Smart Africa - Accelerating the digital transformation in Africa
activities.description:
Context: 

Africa?s growing digital economy holds significant potential for economic progress and technological innovation. While sub-Saharan Africa has the fastest-growing internet usage rate in the world, only 25 per cent of the continent?s population is currently online. This is mainly due to a lack of digital infrastructure, which drives up internet costs. Improved internet access promotes business development, boosts competitiveness, facilitates access to knowledge, and enables broader participation in economic and social development. For this reason, Germany is investing in cooperation with Smart Africa, an alliance of 40 African countries. The goal is to facilitate access to new markets, encourage trade and investment with Africa, and stimulate local economic growth.

Objective: 

An African digital single market is facilitating cross-border trade, promoting investment in the digital economy, improving access to technology, boosting economic growth and driving social participation.

Approach: 

The project works with Smart Africa on the implementation of digital strategies and technologies, shapes organisational development, and connects stakeholders to form new partnerships

activities.title: Green Communication in Multi-Relay Wireless Networks
activities.description: We propose a project on an environment-friendly multi-relay wireless network. In our project, multiple coordinated relays are used to satisfy the users quality-of-service requirements, with minimum impacts on the environment. The main objectives of the proposal are to improve the power efficiency, increase the portion of renewable energy in the wireless networks and develop carbon-reducing systems. To improve the power efficiency, we perform adaptive power allocation, harvest the required energy from renewable energy resources/interference and implement the power amplifiers properly. To cope with global warming and facilitate sustainable development, we add the radio pollution into the problem formulation, as a minimization goal. Advance mathematical tools, such as machine learning, game theory and stochastic geometry, are used for joint relay selection and power allocation. Compared to all current wireless networks, our project is a new paradigm as we change the interference from the most undesirable factor to something good improving the power efficiency. activities.title: AI4D Africa & AI4COVID with IDRC - AI4D Africa with IDRC
activities.description:
AI4D Africa

The program Artificial Intelligence for Development (AI4D) Africa aims to build and support policy, research capacity, and innovations to spur responsible artificial intelligence (AI) development in Africa. Responsible AI strives to be inclusive, rights-based and sustainable.

The future of AI on the African continent, however, is not yet written, and the policies and practices put in place now will greatly shape the flow of benefits and harms from AI.

AI4D will strengthen and promote scientific multidisciplinary AI research in primarily low-income countries in Africa; strengthen low-income countries own research AI capacity; and support sustainable innovation and research systems in low-income countries in Africa with the aim of reaching a critical mass of highly qualified AI researchers.

AI4D will strengthen policies and regulation for AI to be ethical and rights based and have a regulatory framework for the African context that can both stimulate innovation and minimize risks (for example, for human rights).

activities.title: Enabling communication for influence for the Artificial Intelligence for Development in Africa program
activities.description: Strategic communication activities are essential to ensure that the Artificial Intelligence for Development (AI4D) Africa program achieves its objectives. This project seeks to enhance the reach and impact of the program by constructing and implementing an AI4D Africa program communications strategy and funding key communication activities. These activities include the AI4D Africa conference and webinar series, research publications, and supporting an online presence.

activities.title: Artificial Intelligence for Development Africa: Capacity development
activities.description:
This project will support the Artificial Intelligence for Development Africa (AI4D Africa) partnership by covering the operational costs for the partnership, including salaries and benefits, office costs, and travel for IDRC staff. Separate project approval documents will authorize the execution of individual research projects and activities related to program governance, communication, and evaluation. 

AI4D Africa is a partnership between the Swedish International Cooperation Development Agency and IDRC, with a joint investment of CA$18.1 million over four years. AI4D Africa supports policy, innovations, and expanded leadership to spur responsible AI development in Africa. The vision of the program is one where AI empowers Africans to have a more inclusive, prosperous, and greener future.

activities.title: Clinical field studies for point-of-care diagnostics using miniature microscopy scanners
activities.description: We have developed a low-cost miniaturized microscopy scanner that digitizes patient samples at high magnification and transfers the generated virtual slides over mobile networks. Our central server receives the virtual slides and allows the biological samples to be remotely analyzed by automated computer vision or visually assessed by a human observer. A proof-of-concept study supported by the Swedish Research Council has been conducted in 2014-2015 and shown the method to be feasible.  We now plan to implement the novel multipurpose diagnostic platform in two settings in Tanzania: 1) As a diagnostic method for detection of malaria in blood samples obtained from patients presenting with fever at the primary health care level and 2) as a diagnostic and monitoring method for detection of soil-transmitted helminthes and schistosomiasis in stool and urine obtained from schoolchildren within a transmission surveillance survey. activities.title: AI4D- International Development Research Centre (IDRC) -Project Funds to support Outputs 1- 5
activities.description:
The project will work to create the desired impact – an inclusive responsible and inclusive AI ecosystem that improves the quality of life for all in Africa and beyond – through five main areas of work: 
a.	AI Safety, Policy and Governance Research: 
i.	Support and capacity strengthening for African researchers generating AI knowledge and evidence to influence policy at the national, regional and international levels.
ii.	Funding high-quality (gender and disability sensitive, locally driven) evidence on AI governance and regulation and the socio-economic and political effects of AI.
b.	Data: Support and fund the increased availability, findability, sustainability of relevant, machine learning ready datasets.
c.	Talent and Skills: Support multi-disciplinary AI labs and networks, including the financing of PhDs.
d.	Innovation: Responsible AI Innovations are generated that address development challenges.

activities.description: This component holds core programme funds where other projects that enter implementation can draw down funding from.

activities.title: 'AI Accelerator' -Scaling -AI4D
activities.description: This project aims to facilitate the transition from innovative AI solutions to scalable applications that address development challenges in sub-Saharan Africa and Indo-Pacific . A dedicated AI Accelerator will be established to identify and support sustainable AI initiatives. The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) is allocating up to £5 million of the total programme budget for this purpose. This initiative will involve collaboration with other donors and private sector partners to pool resources and expertise. Together, we will select a suitable partner to deliver the AI Accelerator, ensuring that the supported AI solutions are impactful and sustainable in addressing key development issues in the region.

activities.title: Next GenAI Cures Platform
activities.description: AI Co-Scientists – agentic AI tools for scientific hypothesis generation coupled with domain-specific models (e.g., protein design tools) – are proliferating rapidly, but the field lacks robust ways of determining what works, when, and why, which risks wasting time, effort, and resource on tools that are not fit-for-purpose, ultimately slowing scientific progress. This programme aims to address this problem by creating: (1) a living landscape map of Co-Scientist tools, (2) an openly published benchmark (i.e., a suite of automated evaluations) to test the performance of Co-Scientist tools on a range of relevant tasks, and (3) a light-touch secretariat to help FCDO and its partners implement Co-Scientist workflows to accelerate discovery. In parallel, we will collaborate with FCDO’s extensive subject matter expert bench to demonstrate the potential impact of best-in-class AI Co-Scientists by applying them to address three critical global health challenges: novel therapeutics design to address the growing global burden of mental health issues (e.g., a new druggable target); novel susceptibility testing for antimicrobial resistance (e.g., a low-cost and stable point-of-care susceptibil

activities.title: AI for Development Science Breakthroughs
activities.description: This inception programme will run three to five collaborative projects to test how far AI can accelerate breakthroughs on priority global challenges, such as weather prediction for climate adaptation and early warning, drug discovery and bioengineering resilient crops, through providing expertise, partnerships and small, targeted catalytic funding to grow the evidence base. The programme will leverage FCDO’s convening power and thought leadership to crowd in more investment and ensure those pushing the scientific frontier on global development challenges can benefit from and further the evidence on cutting edge AI approaches.

activities.title: Machine learning for digital diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance
activities.description:
If action is not taken, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) will cost $100 trillion and claim 10 million lives annually by 2050. The factors driving AMR extend beyond human healthcare, with implications in veterinary medicine, agriculture, and the environment. New and improved approaches for tackling AMR include better monitoring, rational drug use, different business models to generate antibiotics, innovation at all levels, and most importantly, a global approach. 

This project assembles a transnational team (Canada, China, Finland, France) to apply new machine learning approaches for faster diagnosis and better monitoring of resistance. The initial focus will be on two major global pathogens that have developed multi-drug resistance: Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Streptococcus pneumoniae. The research team will develop machine learning that can orient treatment selection by assessing the level of resistance, providing a rationale for generating novel antibiotics, and assisting in the surveillance of human and livestock antimicrobial resistance.  

This is one of five IDRC-funded projects developed through the Joint Programming Initiative on Antimicrobial Resistance (JPIAMR), an internat

activities.title: A Bird’s-Eye View on Agricultural Transformation in sub-Saharan Africa: An analysis of living standards indicators
activities.description: The last major area in the world where poverty and all of its related issues seem intractable is sub-Saharan Africa. It has long been a problem that fundamental and detailed data regarding development indicators and their distribution over space and time and among different segments of the population are unavailable. This is especially a concern in rural areas and among the farming population. In this project we address longstanding and unresolved questions in development research regarding the distributional effects of rural transformations, poverty and production levels. We do this through an innovative framework featuring a new application of artificial intelligence techniques. More precisely, we apply machine learning to satellite imagery along with more conventional panel survey data. activities.title: A Bird’s-Eye View on Agricultural Transformation in sub-Saharan Africa: An analysis of living standards indicators
activities.description: The last major area in the world where poverty and all of its related issues seem intractable is sub-Saharan Africa. It has long been a problem that fundamental and detailed data regarding development indicators and their distribution over space and time and among different segments of the population are unavailable. This is especially a concern in rural areas and among the farming population. In this project we address longstanding and unresolved questions in development research regarding the distributional effects of rural transformations, poverty and production levels. We do this through an innovative framework featuring a new application of artificial intelligence techniques. More precisely, we apply machine learning to satellite imagery along with more conventional panel survey data. This is the first study of its kind and combines expertise from distant disciplines such as physics, development research and remote sensing in a cross-disciplinary effort.This innovative approach will also provide a real-life contribution to addressing a practical problem of collecting statistics on the ground in developing countries that lack infrastructure or administrative resources. activities.title: Leverage avocado genetic resources for the sustainable socioeconomic development of rural communities in Tanzania
activities.description: Avocado (Persea americana Mill.) is becoming a top fruit commodity worldwide. It is therefore a promising plant resource to improve farmers’ income and nutrition. However, its genetic resources have limitedly been explored and utilized in secondary diversity genepools such as Southeast Africa’s. Therefore, the overall purpose of this starting grant proposal is to harness the genetic and ecological diversity of avocado resources for adaptation to climate change and farmers’ wellbeing in Tanzania, a secondary center of avocado diversity. We hypothesize that adaptation in response to local ecological opportunities and inter-racial hybridization may sustainably source the rapid growth of avocado plantations in Tanzania. During four years, a total of 900 trees, and their progenies, will be monitored through extensive field surveys, greenhouse experiments, whole-genome re-sequencing (WGR), and last-generation analytical approaches such as genomic prediction and machine learning. This effort will throw lights into the standing variation of avocado resources in Tanzania, as well as into innovative ways to leverage such diversity. activities.title: More and better statistics with reliable labour market information systems
activities.description:
The following are the major global deliverables and activities of the ILO in this policy area.
(1) a capacity-building and technical assistance programme to support Member States in adopting the latest statistical standards endorsed by the International Conference of Labour Statisticians (www.ilo.org/icls) on key labour market variables like work, work relationships and informality, and in producing and disseminating statistics in relation to SDG indicators under the ILO’s custodianship and those related to decent work.
(2) strengthened support to develop labour market information systems integrated in national statistical systems with increased capacity to analyse decent work trends, including by carrying out regional training activities with the Turin Centre.
(3) a consolidated and enhanced ILOSTAT database based on an updated and enlarged harmonized microdata repository.

activities.title: Leveraging AI and data analytics to counter misinformation in the MENA: experimenting with data patterns on social media in Arabic content
activities.description:
An “infodemic” of misinformation has infected the global online media landscape with increasing virulence over the last five years. As new variants of COVID-19 thrive thanks in part to these same forces, it is critical that we dedicate resources to effectively counter online misinformation. This need is particularly urgent in the Arab world (the Middle East and North Africa, or MENA), where a dearth of independent media has forced citizens to rely on social-media platforms for news. Globally, very few resources have been dedicated to advancing evidence-based research or artificial-intelligence tools to detect and counter the spread of misinformation in the Arabic language.   

This research project seeks to evaluate the current landscape of misinformation in Arabic by aggregating data from Arabic fact-checking initiatives into a first-of-its-kind multilateral database. Against this data set, the team will perform analysis using natural language processing techniques to detect broad patterns behind how misinformation affects minority groups, public sentiment towards misinformation and patterns behind its propagation.

activities.title: Pulse Lab Jakarta Phase II
activities.description:
Pulse Lab Jakarta (PLJ) is one of the first data innovation labs in the Asia Pacific to harness big data, artificial intelligence and human-centred design for sustainable development and humanitarian action. Established in 2012, PLJ is a joint initiative of the United Nations, through United Nations Global Pulse and the Government of Indonesia, through its Ministry of National Development Planning (BAPPENAS). 

This second phase of investment would have three main aims: 
1. To equip partners with fit-for-purpose methods and data tools needed to respond faster and more effectively to complex challenges; 
2. To strengthen demand for harnessing insights from non-conventional data sources; and 
3. To catalyse positive changes in Indonesia’s data ecosystem.

activities.title: TCPF: Machine learning for rice yield modelling
activities.description: To enhance capacities within the National Institute of Statistics (NIS) and other agricultural stakeholders in Cambodia to effectively utilize advanced data analytics such as machine learning for agricultural planning and management.

activities.title: Geocomputation Research: Using satellite data and machine learning to detect urban damage during natural hazard and conflict
activities.description: The purpose of this project is to build the prototype for a platform capable of delivering accurate and timely damage assessments in the aftermath of natural disasters and armed conflict.

activities.title: Pulse Lab Jakarta Phase 2
activities.description:
Pulse Lab Jakarta (PLJ) was data innovation initiative in the Asia–Pacific region. The Lab developed data driven and AI enabled prototypes to support sustainable development and humanitarian action, drawing on big data analytics and human centred design. PLJ was established as a partnership between the United Nations, through UN Global Pulse, and the Government of Indonesia, through the Ministry of National Development Planning (BAPPENAS).

PLJ contributed to several Government of Indonesia priorities, including strengthening the Ministry of Health’s analytical capacity during the COVID 19 response; supporting national efforts to build a more inclusive digital economy, particularly for vulnerable and underserved groups; and assisting Bappenas to establish a low carbon advanced analytics function to help ministries to analyse climate forecasts and develop long term, evidence based climate policies.

activities.title: UN Global Pulse
activities.description: The UN Global Pulse Asia Pacific (UNGP-AP) is a data innovation facility that supports policymakers in the region to use big data, artificial intelligence (AI), strategic foresight and behavioural science to design innovative evidence-led policy and programs. UNGP-AP provides services such as: translating AI and big data into programs e.g., dashboard/ innovative data platforms; providing technical assistance (TA) including access to international experts on big data and training on data analytics for improved data governance; as well as exploratory research using traditional and non-traditional data. The key priority areas include sea level rise mapping and dashboards for better targeting for Indonesia’s flagship program on nutritious meals. The UN Global Pulse – Asia Pacific (UNGP-AP) builds on the successful partnership model spanning over a decade between Indonesia, Australia and the United Nations under the Pulse Lab Jakarta portfolio.

activities.title: Addressing Vaccine Misinformation with an Inoculation Chatbot
activities.description: To protect populations against viral misinformation, the implementing partner used behavioral science to design an inoculation chatbot, through which interactive software guides users through narrative, games, and experiential learning that pre-bunks misinformation, equipping users with the skills required to be less susceptible to misinformation. Misinformation about the SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) pandemicranging from rumors about false cures to harmful conspiracieshas spread rapidly through populations via social media and other channels. This spread poses a serious challenge for public health officials working to protect their populations with effective, safe vaccines. Vaccine hesitancy remains strong in Uzbekistan, with only 47.9 percent of its 34 million residents vaccinated against COVID-19. The inoculation chatbot will be a free service and cost less to run than traditional media and short message services. The implementing partner is partnering with the Government of Uzbekistan to pilot the chatbot, and will conduct a randomized controlled trial to identify whether the chatbot helps users better spot manipulation techniques, reduces willingness to share manipulation techniques,

activities.title: Using Machine Learning to Reduce HIV Treatment Interruptions
activities.description: Approximately 39 million people were living with HIV/AIDS worldwide at the end of 2022. While great strides have been made in increasing access to treatment, interruption in treatment remains a persistent problem that can result in viral rebound, disease advancement, and premature mortality. A study in Akwa Ibom, Nigeria found the treatment retention rate for people living with HIV/AIDS to be just 68 percent after one year, significantly lower than the benchmark of 98 percent set by the Presidents Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) in Nigeria. To increase the treatment retention rate, FHI 360 developed and piloted a machine learning algorithm to identify people likely to interrupt treatment using patient data available through HIV/AIDS programs. Once the algorithm identifies people likely to interrupt treatment, providers can offer tailored care to address barriers that may prevent them from adhering to treatment. activities.title: Testing and Scaling an Artificial Intelligence-Based Functional Literacy Program
activities.description: Many of Brazils 28 million public school studentsespecially those from economically disadvantaged familiesare unprepared to attend university and enter the workforce. Nearly one-third of 15-to-64-year-old Brazilians are functionally illiterate, meaning they lack the reading, writing, and math skills required for everyday life. To help solve this literacy gap at scale, the implementing partner developed an artificial intelligence (AI)powered educational program that engages students in the classroom and supports teachers by providing specific, prompt feedback on writing submissions. The system goes beyond spelling and basic grammar to support students skills in diction, organization and flow, reading comprehension, and other aspects to promote functional literacy. A smaller-scale randomized controlled trial (RCT) found that using the system in the final year of high school improved students essay scores on Brazils college entrance exam by 0.1 standard deviations (or 17 points out of a possible 1,000), compared with the control group, results that may reduce inequalities between public and private schools. activities.title: ARCED Foundation: Aureolin Research, Consultancy, and Expertise Development: Using Satellite Imagery to Reduce Air Pollution
activities.description: In Bangladesh, air pollution shortens the average person's life by 6.9 years. The country's average annual particulate concentration is almost 74, nearly 15 times the WHO guideline of five. Exposure to air pollution causes life-threatening diseases such as asthma, cancer, and heart disease. In 2014, the Government of Bangladesh introduced a regulation that makes a primary source of pollutants brick kilns illegal near population centers, schools, and medical facilities. However, kilns continue to operate in violation of the regulation due to insufficient enforcement, putting the health of millions of people at risk. In 2022, Bangladesh's Department of the Environment (DoE) found that 60 percent of the country's 7,881 brick kilns operate illegally without environmental clearance and that up to 58 percent of fine particles (commonly referred to as PM2.5) in Dhaka air come from brick kilns. activities.title: AI-based Entrepreneurship Training Pilot
activities.description: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) represent about 90 percent of businesses worldwide and generate a significant portion of jobs and economic output, especially in developing countries. Research has shown that certain business and management practices are associated with higher rates of enterprise survival and sales growth. Governments and donors spend significant resources to provide training to help entrepreneurs implement these practices. While such training can be effective, it is often also intensive and expensive, and therefore limited in scale. Leveraging recent advances in large language models, Hacer Peru has developed a training, mentoring, and consulting tool called MAIA that aims to provide guidance on leading business and management practices to small business owners at a fraction of the cost. Delivered via WhatsApp, MAIA draws on information specific to the needs of MSMEs in Peru and responds in real-time to questions and challenges faced by entrepreneurs. activities.title: Enhanced enabling environment to promote the development and creation of green, sustainable and resilient enterprises in the entire value/supply chain, and particularly for MSMEs.
activities.description:
PHL104 strengthens the enabling environment for sustainable and resilient enterprises, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), to maximize productive, remunerative, freely chosen and sustainable work. It supports the MSME Development Plan for 2023-2028 and the Labour and Employment Plan (LEP) 2023–2028’s priority enterprise sustainability. The Country Programme Outcome (CPO) aligns with national strategies such as the National AI Strategy for the Philippines, the National AI Strategy Roadmap 2.0, the E-Government Masterplan, the E-Commerce Roadmap, the Philippine Export Development Plan and the National Digital Workforce Competitiveness Act. The CPO also supports two flagship legislative initiatives of the Philippine government: Tatak Pinoy (Proudly Filipino) Act and Trabaho Para sa Bayan Act. Furthermore, it also contributes to the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2024–2028’s priority on sustainable economic development and decent work, by improving institutions and systems that foster a competitive, inclusive, and digitally integrated business environment.
